extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, and third-party reexamination requesters (practitioners involved in ex parte reexamination)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements governing ex parte patent reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 301–305 and pertinent 37 CFR rules, including fees, filings, service, scope of reexamination, examiner treatment, and evidentiary limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess claims fees (37 CFR 1.20(c)) apply only to submission of new (excess) claims presented in an amendment (on or after Dec. 8, 2004). If amendment merely revises existing claims and does not provide any new claim, no claim fee is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees apply only to added claims that are 'new/excess'. Examples illustrate application based on independent and total claim counts relative to the patent being reexamined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent excess claims fee condition (37 CFR 1.20(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The independent claims fee must be paid for each independent claim in excess of three AND in excess of the number of independent claims in the patent being reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both limits must be exceeded by the amendment (i.e., amendment must increase independent claims to be more than three and more than the original patent's independent claims). Example: if patent has six independent claims and amendment results in seven independent claims, the fee for the seventh independent claim applies (illustrated in examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Total excess claims fee condition (37 CFR 1.20(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The total claims fee must be paid for each claim (independent or dependent) in excess of twenty AND in excess of the number of claims in the patent being reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment must increase total claims beyond both limits. Example: in a patent with 30 claims, adding an 11th new claim (when 10 were canceled) that increases total to 31 triggers the total excess claims fee for the thirty-first claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation exclusion — disclaimed or previously cancelled claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim disclaimed under 35 U.S.C. 253 and 37 CFR 1.321(a) as of the date of filing of the reexamination request is not considered a claim in the patent for excess claims fee calculations. Same for claims canceled via prior Reexamination Certificate, reissue, or Certificate of Correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such disclaimed/canceled claims are excluded when comparing the amendment's claim counts to the patent's original counts for fee applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee deficiency procedure (PTOL-475)
rubrics_metrics.description: If required excess claims fees are not paid with presentation of excess claims, a Notice of Defective Paper (PTOL-475) will be issued setting a one-month period to correct the fee deficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An extension to correct the deficiency may be requested under 37 CFR 1.550(c). If unpaid within the time set, the reexamination will be terminated under 37 CFR 1.550(e) effecting abandonment per 37 CFR 1.20(c)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party requester reply timing (37 CFR 1.535)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to the patent owner's statement under § 1.530 may be filed by the ex parte reexamination requester within two months from the date of service of the patent owner's statement; this two-month period is statutory (35 U.S.C. 304) and not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner does not file a statement under § 1.530, no reply or other submission from the requester will be considered. The reply must be served on the patent owner in accordance with § 1.248.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted content of requester reply
rubrics_metrics.description: The requester’s reply need not be limited to issues raised in the patent owner's statement; it may include additional prior art patents and printed publications and may raise any issue appropriate for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issues raised in the reply that are within the scope of reexamination will be treated by the examiner; issues outside scope should be treated pursuant to 37 CFR 1.552(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: No further filings by requester after reply
rubrics_metrics.description: The third party requester is not permitted to file any further papers after the reply to the patent owner's statement; any further papers will not be considered and will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner cannot file papers on behalf of requester to circumvent rules; such submissions are inappropriate and will be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and limit on pre-examination submissions (37 CFR 1.540)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to timely file or serve documents set forth in §§ 1.530 or 1.535 may result in refusal of consideration. No submissions other than the statement (1.530) and reply (1.535) will be considered prior to examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the regulation uses 'may', untimely filings can be expected to be refused; untimely submissions ordinarily will not be considered or placed of record and will be returned to sender (except certain untimely patent owner papers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of service requirement for papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed that require proof of service but include none may be denied consideration. If no proof of service is included, the reexamination clerk should inquire whether service was made; if no service, the paper is placed in the file but not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2266.03 and 2267 for further discussion. Documents must reflect service or may be refused consideration by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner consideration of properly filed submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Once reexamination is ordered, any submissions properly filed and served in accordance with 37 CFR 1.530 and 1.535 will be considered by the examiner when preparing the first Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner guidance for consideration of proposed amendments to specification/claims is in 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j); for patent owner statements see 1.530(c); for requester reply see 1.535. New issues raised by requester within scope will be addressed in Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of issues outside scope
rubrics_metrics.description: If an issue raised by a third party requester in the reply is not within the scope of reexamination, it should be treated pursuant to 37 CFR 1.552(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issues other than those based on patents/printed publications or 35 U.S.C. 112 for added/deleted matter will not be resolved in reexamination; examiner notes such issues in next Office action and patent owner may consider reissue application for those issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of ex parte reexamination — general (35 U.S.C. 305; 37 CFR 1.550)
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing periods expire, reexamination is conducted according to initial examination procedures (35 U.S.C. 132, 133) and results in issuance of a reexamination certificate under § 1.570. Patent owner may propose amendments or new claims to distinguish over cited prior art, but no proposed amendment or new claim that enlarges scope will be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings (including appeals) will be conducted with special dispatch. A full search will not routinely be made by examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response periods and extensions for patent owner (37 CFR 1.550(b),(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner will be given at least thirty days to respond to any Office action. Time for action by patent owner will be extended only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified; extension requests must be filed on or before due date and must be accompanied by the petition fee in § 1.17(g). Filing the request alone does not effect the extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.304(a) for extensions for appeals to Federal Circuit or commencing civil actions. Extensions are discretionary and require petition/fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to file timely response
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response to an Office action or required interview statement, the ex parte reexamination proceeding will be terminated and the Director will issue a certificate under § 1.570 in accordance with the last action of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination/abandonment procedures follow 37 CFR 1.550(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of delayed responses (petitions under 1.137)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a response is not timely filed, delay may be excused if shown unavoidable (petition under 1.137(a)), or the response may be accepted if delay was unintentional (petition under 1.137(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must comply with the specified 1.137 provisions and supporting showing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service obligation for documents filed after requester’s initial filing
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing of a request for ex parte reexamination by a third party requester, any document filed by either the patent owner or the requester must be served on the other party in the manner provided by § 1.248; the document must reflect service or it may be refused consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to reflect service can result in refusal of consideration; the reexamination requester will be sent copies of Office actions issued during the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: End of active participation by third-party requester
rubrics_metrics.description: Active participation of the ex parte reexamination requester ends with the reply pursuant to § 1.535; no further submissions on behalf of the requester will be acknowledged or considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further third-party submissions will not be considered unless they are (1) in accordance with § 1.510 or § 1.535, or (2) entered in the patent file prior to the date of the order for ex parte reexamination pursuant to § 1.525.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of third-party submissions after order (37 CFR 1.501(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions by third parties filed after the date of the order for ex parte reexamination must meet the requirements of and will be treated in accordance with § 1.501(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such late third-party submissions have a specific statutory/regulatory path and are not freely admitted into the ex parte proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte nature and limits on third-party argumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Once ex parte reexamination is ordered, proceedings are ex parte (no further active participation by third-party requester allowed) to prevent introduction of multiple arguments/issues beyond intent of 35 U.S.C. 305 and to reduce harassment of patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner may not file papers on behalf of requester; court-ordered filings prepared by third parties and filed by patent owner are inappropriate and will be returned (citing Emerson Elec. v. Davoil).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's search and citation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A full search will not routinely be made by the examiner. Citations submitted to the patent file prior to issuance of the order for reexamination will be considered by the examiner during reexamination. Reexamination proceeds even if the order copy to patent owner is returned undelivered (37 CFR 1.11(c) notice is constructive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of patent owner response will not delay reexamination; examiner ordinarily is same as who decided to grant the request unless a petition under 1.515(c) changes examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary sources of prior art in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary source of prior art are the patents and printed publications cited in the request for ex parte reexamination; examiner must also consider patents/printed publications cited by other reexamination requesters (1.510/1.915), cited in owner/requester statements if complying with 1.98, cited under duty of disclosure 1.555 (if complying with 1.98), discovered by examiner, of record from earlier examination, or of record from any 1.501 submission prior to the order (if complying with 1.98).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reexamination file must clearly indicate which prior art patents/printed publications the examiner has considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing of prior art citations (PTO-892 etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner must list on form PTO-892 (or equivalent forms PTO-1449, PTO/SB/08A/08B, PTO/SB/42) all prior art patents or printed publications properly cited and relied upon by the requester or otherwise of record/discovered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All citations listed on PTO-892, and all citations not lined-through on related forms, will be printed on the reexamination certificate under 'References Cited.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for entry and citation on reexamination certificate (compliance with 37 CFR 1.98)
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission of patents/publications is entitled to entry and citation in the reexamination certificate when it complies with 37 CFR 1.98 and is submitted by: (A) patent owner in 1.530 statement; (B) requester in 1.535 reply; (C) any party prior to order under 1.501; and/or (D) patent owner under duty of disclosure 1.555.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with 1.98 is required for the item to be of record and printed on the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reexamination — limited bases (37 CFR 1.552(a)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims will be examined on the basis of patents or printed publications and, with respect to subject matter added or deleted, on the basis of 35 U.S.C. 112. Claims in reexamination will not be permitted to enlarge scope. Issues other than those indicated (patents/printed publications and 112 for added matter) will not be resolved in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such other issues are raised, examiner will note them in the next Office action and patent owner may consider reissue to have them resolved; new/amended claims are examined to ensure scope not broadened per 35 U.S.C. 305.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections limited to patents/printed publications and appropriate statutory provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections in reexamination proceedings may only be made on the basis of prior art patents or printed publications, applied under appropriate portions of 35 U.S.C. 102 and/or 103; rejections based on other matters (public use/sale, inventorship, 35 U.S.C. 101, fraud, etc.) will not be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if such matters rely on a prior art patent/printed publication, they must be applied under correct 102/103 provisions when making a rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously considered prior art and substantial new question of patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: After reexamination is ordered based on a proper substantial new question (SNQ), the propriety of making a rejection based on prior art previously considered by the Office is governed by MPEP § 2258.01; combinations of previously considered art with newly cited art can support an SNQ (In re Hiniker).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court precedent supports that combinations of old and new art can justify reexamination even if some art was before the original examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening patents/printed publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections may be made based on intervening patents or printed publications where the claims under reexamination are entitled only to the patent's filing date and are not supported by an earlier application whose filing date is claimed (e.g., under 35 U.S.C. 120 situations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intervening patents/publications are treated as prior art per In re Ruscetta, In re van Langenhoven, and MPEP § 201.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting — consideration in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Double patenting is appropriate for consideration in reexamination both as a basis for ordering reexamination and during subsequent examination; examiner should determine whether double patenting raises a substantial new question and whether a double patenting rejection is appropriate during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double patenting may exist where the reexamined patent and another patent/application contain conflicting claims and (A) are filed by same inventive entity; (B) filed by different entities having a common inventor; (C) filed by a common assignee; and/or (D) result from joint research agreement activities as defined in 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(3). Post-2004/date-specific conditions and terminal disclaimer remedies are addressed (use form paragraphs 14.23.01, 14.25–14.32 as appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/declarations limited role
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations that explain contents or pertinent dates of prior art patents/printed publications may be considered, but any rejection must be based upon the prior art patents/printed publications as explained — not on the affidavits/declarations per se.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits/declarations can clarify prior art but cannot themselves be the legal basis for rejection absent underlying patents/publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of admissions by patent owner in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissions by the patent owner of record in the file or in a court record may be utilized in combination with a patent or printed publication; an admission by itself may not establish an SNQ but may be used to interpret/modify prior art in determining obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions can come from patent file or litigation record; third parties may not submit admissions made outside the record. Case law supports use of admissions to determine scope/content of prior art (e.g., Ex parte Seiko, Kimbell, McGaughey).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim interpretation in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims are given the broadest reasonable interpretation consistent with the specification; limitations in the specification are not read into the claims. For expired patents (not subject to amendment), a policy of narrow construction favoring validity should be applied. The presumption of validity (35 U.S.C. 282) does not apply in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In re Yamamoto and other authorities govern broadest-reasonable-interpretation in reexamination; for expired patents apply narrow construction (In re Papst-Motoren).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112 for new/added matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Where new claims are presented or where any part of the specification/claims/drawings is added or deleted in reexamination, those changes are examined for compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures that added subject matter meets written description/enabling/definiteness requirements; see MPEP § 2270 for handling new matter.
